text.p: Edison Brothers Stores Inc said Thursday it postponed to September 9 a confirmation hearing before a U.S. Bankruptcy Court to allow the company time to resolve $40 million in outstanding claims by the Internal Revenue Service.
The hearing was to be held today.
The retailer said the postponement should not affect its plans to emerge from bankruptcy early this fall.
Edison Brothers filed for bankruptcy in November 1995.
The IRS claims involve several different tax issues and are disputed by the company, it said. Details were not disclosed.

"While we would have preferred not to reschedule the hearing, Edison has moved through the Chapter 11 process quickly and we feel confident that dedicating a few extra weeks to negotiate this matter should facilitate the confirmation hearing in September," said Chief Executive Officer Alan Miller in a news release.
Edison Brothers operates more than 1,600 stores in the U.S., Canada, Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands.
